diagnosis.primary_bottleneck: ten stable-core outer fits each contain five 128-tree random-forest relevance fits; the component random forests were serialized by n_jobs=1
diagnosis.secondary_bottleneck: all 1959 matrix predictors were encoded and passed to both the LLM candidate prompt and every supervised stable-core component

feature_availability_filter.rule: retain predictor when fold-1 DEV-training missing rate <= 0.90
feature_availability_filter.reference_scope: earliest frozen DEV training fold only

maximum_performance_controls.reason_for_single_outer_fit: bound peak memory while each random forest parallelizes its trees across all logical CPUs
maximum_performance_controls.memory_recovery: existing supervised controller stops an owned worker at the authenticated memory boundary and restarts from the last sealed selection or evaluation checkpoint

local_microbenchmark.benchmark_scope: first 10000 authenticated fold-1 training rows, exact 1068-feature retained universe, 32 trees, otherwise frozen RF parameters
local_microbenchmark.interpretation: representative scheduling benchmark only; full-fold scaling is limited by memory bandwidth and is not guaranteed to equal the microbenchmark

checkpoint_compatibility.reason: the missingness filter changes the candidate universe and the shared LLM prompt/ranking, so mixing v2 folds 1-2 with v3 folds 3-5 would invalidate like-for-like five-fold results

estimated_runtime.basis: observed 8.49x all-core RF microbenchmark, 45.5 percent candidate reduction, prior fold timings, growing training-fold row counts, and conservative memory-bandwidth allowance
